tldr_label: TL;DR: Ukraine talks open in Abu Dhabi, oil drops below $90, France blames Iran for a supermarket hack, and the House prepares a Hegseth vote

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: US, Russian and Ukrainian delegations opened two days of security-focused talks in Abu Dhabi, the first trilateral round in months. Russian strikes on the power grid continued. [[TAG:warning:modest hopes]]

tldr_bullets.label: Oil
tldr_bullets.body: CNBC reported that Brent fell below $90 for the first time since August as traders bet on a US-Iran deal. Asian stocks rallied. [[TAG:success:de-escalation bet]]

tldr_bullets.label: France and Iran
tldr_bullets.body: Paris summoned Iran's ambassador and will seek EU sanctions after prosecutors blamed the Revolutionary Guard for a cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration. [[TAG:danger:cyber sabotage]]

tldr_bullets.label: Washington
tldr_bullets.body: The House may vote by Wednesday on Massie's impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Hegseth. The Senate races in Alaska and Mississippi remain uncalled. [[TAG:warning:vote pending]]

tldr_bullets.label: Nvidia
tldr_bullets.body: Nvidia fell 4.27% on Monday while the broader market rallied, after its board opened an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a woman US officials reportedly believe was a Chinese intelligence asset. [[TAG:danger:governance probe]]

sections.title: Ukraine: Talks Open in Abu Dhabi
sections.summary: First trilateral round since February focuses on security guarantees as strikes continue

paragraphs.heading: The Table
paragraphs.body: NPR, NBC News and CBS News reported that US-mediated talks between the United States, Russia and Ukraine began in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday. The National said the two days of sessions focus on security guarantees and a longer-term security arrangement between Russia and Europe. CNN described the round as a restart after roughly nine months. ABC News reported that President Trump says the war can 'end soon.' [[TAG:info:two-day round]]

paragraphs.heading: Europe in the Room
paragraphs.body: According to The National, representatives of Britain, France, Germany and Italy, along with NATO and the European Commission, met the Ukrainian and US delegations in Abu Dhabi before the trilateral session. Russia had objected to European involvement in the three-way format. The Washington Post reported that Putin aide Vladimir Medinsky leads Moscow's delegation. [[TAG:warning:Moscow objects]]

paragraphs.heading: Territory Gap
paragraphs.body: CBS News reported that Zelensky continues to reject Russian demands that Ukraine give up territory Russia has not taken on the battlefield. US officials framed the round as a first step that could build momentum. One former US ambassador quoted in coverage said expectations should be 'very modest.' [[TAG:danger:core dispute unresolved]]

paragraphs.heading: Grid Under Fire
paragraphs.body: France 24 and Al Jazeera reported that weekend Russian strikes cut power to hundreds of thousands of people. DTEK said more than 600,000 residents of Dnipropetrovsk region lost electricity. Ukrinform reported that Ukrenergo recorded attacks on energy infrastructure in eight regions overnight into Tuesday, with hourly outage schedules across most of the country. CNN said analysts see a campaign aimed at Ukraine's economy ahead of winter. [[TAG:danger:power cuts]]

sections.title: Iran: Talks, Oil and a Cyber Row
sections.summary: Brent drops below $90 on deal hopes; France blames the Revolutionary Guard for a fridge hack

paragraphs.heading: Deal Watch
paragraphs.body: CNN reported that Washington and Tehran are negotiating quietly, with Qatar as the main mediator. Bloomberg said on Friday that the two sides had moved closer to a deal, with nuclear issues back on the table. Al Jazeera reported on Monday that Iran is holding to its seven demands, including lifting the US blockade of its southern ports and lifting sanctions, while the US increases military pressure. The outlets differ on how close an agreement is. [[TAG:warning:no deal yet]]

paragraphs.heading: Oil Slides
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that Brent fell below $90 a barrel on Tuesday for the first time since August, on hopes the Iran war will de-escalate. Analysts cited recovering regional oil flows and reports that Iran may soften its position on the Strait of Hormuz. IOL put Brent near $91 mid-morning in South Africa, so quoted prices vary by time of day. [[TAG:success:about 20% lower this month]]

paragraphs.heading: Supermarket Sabotage
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported that France summoned Iran's ambassador on Tuesday to lodge a 'very strong protest.' Paris prosecutors said on Monday that a cyber unit of Iran's Revolutionary Guard was behind an October attack that disabled refrigeration in hundreds of supermarkets. Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said France would seek sanctions at the European level. Reports of the number of stores hit range from about 700 to more than 1,000. The Week said investigators cited Farsi-language traces and Iran-linked IP addresses. No Iranian response appeared in the coverage reviewed. [[TAG:danger:EU sanctions sought]]

sections.title: Israel and Gaza
sections.summary: Eisenkot courts partners, including possibly Netanyahu; storm floods some 70,000 Gaza tents

paragraphs.heading: Coalition Paths
paragraphs.body: NBC News and Fox News reported that factions representing 67 of the Knesset's 120 members recommended Eisenkot. Because he has ruled out relying on Arab-led parties, that tally does not translate into a working majority. Al Jazeera reported that Eisenkot is open to Netanyahu joining his government. ABC News (Australia) set out five ways the talks could end, including Netanyahu receiving the mandate next if Eisenkot fails. Reports differ on the deadline: some cite 28 days plus a possible extension, while Al Jazeera cites six weeks. [[TAG:info:61 needed]]

paragraphs.heading: Gaza Floods
paragraphs.body: La Sicilia and other outlets reported that a storm flooded about 70,000 tents in Gaza and killed at least five people. According to UN humanitarian office figures cited in the reports, children were among the dead. Gaza's Government Media Office accuses Israel of blocking tens of thousands of tents and mobile homes, and Israel has not responded to that claim in the coverage reviewed. Al Jazeera's weekly roundup also documented escalating settler violence in the West Bank. [[TAG:danger:shelter crisis]]

sections.title: Washington
sections.summary: Massie files articles against Hegseth with a vote possible by Wednesday; two Senate races open

paragraphs.heading: Hegseth Articles
paragraphs.body: CBS News reported that Rep. Thomas Massie introduced articles of impeachment on Monday accusing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth of waging war on Iran without congressional authorization. A floor vote is possible this week. According to Yahoo News' live coverage, Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries is a 'hard yes' and Speaker Mike Johnson called impeachment during hostilities 'a terrible, terrible look.' Removal would require 67 Senate votes. [[TAG:warning:House vote pending]]

paragraphs.heading: Count Continues
paragraphs.body: Yahoo News, citing AP tallies, reported that Democrats hold at least 54 Senate seats, with Alaska and Mississippi still uncalled, and 254 House seats, with 19 races uncalled. NBC News said a government funding bill tops Congress's agenda as members return. Punchbowl News said Republicans will also choose a new leader. [[TAG:info:counting continues]]

sections.title: Markets and the Nvidia Probe
sections.summary: Wall Street rallies as Nvidia falls 4%; Tokyo and Seoul surge; US inflation data due

paragraphs.heading: Huang Investigation
paragraphs.body: CBS News and NBC News reported that Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation, led by independent directors with outside counsel, after reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a Chinese intelligence effort. The Washington Post and CNBC said Huang acknowledged an affair with a businesswoman whom US officials reportedly believe was a Chinese Ministry of State Security asset. The board said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised. China's Foreign Ministry called the spy narrative unsubstantiated. CNBC reported bipartisan calls in Congress for an inquiry. [[TAG:danger:board probe]]

paragraphs.heading: Rally Without Nvidia
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that Nvidia closed down 4.27% on Monday. Chartmill and TechFlow reported that the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq each rose more than 2%, led by other chipmakers such as AMD and Broadcom. Vantage Markets put Nvidia's slide since November 4 at about 11%. Nvidia reports quarterly earnings on November 17. [[TAG:warning:index heavyweight lags]]

paragraphs.heading: Asia and CPI
paragraphs.body: JournalArta reported that Japan's Nikkei jumped more than 5% on Tuesday and Australia's ASX 200 rose about 1%, as Asian tech stocks followed Wall Street higher. TipRanks and Yahoo Finance said traders were waiting for the October US consumer price report, due Tuesday morning. [[TAG:info:CPI today]]

sections.title: Taiwan Strait
sections.summary: Taipei says the Liaoning group is running 'area denial' drills; G7 warns against coercion

paragraphs.heading: Area Denial
paragraphs.body: The Japan Times reported that Taiwan's defense minister Koo said on Tuesday that China is conducting 'area denial' drills in the Western Pacific with the Liaoning carrier group and other naval formations. Beijing has not formally announced any exercise. China's defense ministry has previously described the carrier's Western Pacific training as routine and not aimed at any country. Taiwanese officials also reported a sharp increase in Chinese military aircraft around the island. [[TAG:warning:undeclared drills]]

paragraphs.heading: G7 and Carriers
paragraphs.body: The Japan Times reported that G7 foreign ministers meeting in Paris expressed strong opposition to any attempt to change the status quo by force or coercion, including across the Taiwan Strait. Modern Diplomacy and the Western Journal noted that the Liaoning group is moving toward waters where a US carrier is exercising with allied ships. The drills come ahead of next week's APEC summit in Shenzhen. [[TAG:info:APEC next week]]

sections.title: Around the World
sections.summary: COP31 opens without US officials; Turkish steel plant blast kills 16; Pope visits Argentina

paragraphs.heading: COP31
paragraphs.body: UN News reported that the COP31 climate conference opened in Antalya, Türkiye, and runs through November 20, with more than 90,000 participants expected and a leaders' summit on November 11 and 12. The agenda covers loss and damage, the pace of the clean-energy transition, and whether rich countries will meet their finance pledges. Türkiye holds the presidency and Australia's Chris Bowen leads the negotiations. Coverage noted that the US has not sent officials. [[TAG:info:runs to Nov 20]]

paragraphs.heading: Izmir Blast
paragraphs.body: CNN and the Washington Post reported that an explosion at the HABAS steel plant in Aliaga, Izmir province, on Monday killed 16 people and injured 13, according to President Erdogan. Earlier counts from the governor were lower. Initial findings reported in coverage point to a crane falling into an arc furnace during casting. An investigation is under way. [[TAG:danger:16 dead]]

paragraphs.heading: Pope in Argentina
paragraphs.body: CNN reported that Pope Leo XIV, on the first papal visit to Argentina since 1987, urged President Milei to safeguard democracy. Local authorities estimated that about 2.5 million people attended his first Mass in Buenos Aires, according to EWTN's live coverage. Vatican News reported that he visited the San Martín monument. [[TAG:success:first since 1987]]

paragraphs.heading: Africa
paragraphs.body: Africanews reported that a train collision in Egypt killed seven people and injured 125, and that the toll from a migrant boat sinking off Senegal has reached at least 39. In South Africa, Africanews said coalition talks are taking centre stage as the ANC loses ground. [[TAG:warning:coalition talks]]
